meta.title: Eastmere City Libraries — Fine-free pilot readout, 24 months
meta.description: Research readout for the Eastmere library board: 24 months after ending late fines in 11 of 19 branches, late returns fell from 9.1% to 6.4% of loans and 3,800 lapsed members came back, at a cost of €46k a year in lost fines. The board is asked to end fines in all 19 branches.

slides.eyebrow: Eastmere City Libraries · Fine-free pilot, 24 months · Library board · 11 December 2026
slides.heading: Ending late fines brought both books and members back.
slides.lead: 11 fine-free branches compared with the 8 that still charge, November 2024 to October 2026.
slides.notes: Give the answer first. The board can stop after slide 2 and still know the result, the cost and the ask.

slides.heading: Two fine-free years won back books and 3,800 members for €46k

cards.title: Books come back sooner
cards.body: Late returns fell from 9.1% to 6.4% of loans.

cards.title: Members came back
cards.body: 3,800 lapsed members borrowed again; 61% had owed fines.

cards.title: The cost is small
cards.body: €46k a year in lost fines, 0.3% of the €15.2M budget.

slides.heading: We asked whether fines bring books back or keep readers away
slides.lead: Until November 2024 every branch charged €0.20 a day per item, capped at €8.

slides.heading: Three findings
slides.lead: Returns, members, and what it cost.

slides.heading: Late returns fell from 9.1% to 6.4% in fine-free branches
slides.lead: Loans more than 14 days late, % of loans; 11 fine-free branches, 8 kept fines. Source: library records, n = 1.86M loans.
slides.notes: The branches that kept fines barely moved. That control group is why we can say fines, not a citywide trend, made the difference.

slides.quote: I owed €8 on my son's picture books and stayed away for three years. Now we come every Saturday.
slides.by: Survey answer 214 · returning member · Northgate branch
